title: SDK auto argument mapper and graceful stream fallback for function invocation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an ergonomic cross-SDK helper that performs: 1) function schema validation with best-effort coercion for common types, 2) auto-mapping of user arguments (positional, keyword, JSON blobs) to declared function schemas, and 3) a graceful fallback for streaming function responses (resume points / chunk buffering). This work spans Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs and must preserve consistent behavior across languages for error semantics, retry idempotency, and developer ergonomics. The goal is to reduce integration friction for users implementing tool/function calling while avoiding surprising coercions that could lead to silent correctness bugs.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-language helper API exists in Python/TS/Go with consistent function signatures and docs
Schema validator enforces required fields and types but supports numeric & boolean coercion from strings for common client inputs
Auto-mapper supports: positional->named mapping, flat JSON object mapping, nested object coercion up to two levels
Streaming invocation helper can resume from last-acknowledged chunk with stable resume token and preserves KV cache for in-flight calls
Idempotency keys are attached correctly for retryable invocations and logged in tracing
Unit and integration tests cover validation edge-cases, retry semantics, and streaming resume in all three SDKs
Documentation examples (Python, TS, Go) published in SDK repo and Console docs
Performance impact on median invocation latency < 6ms in common warm-path for Python/TS; Go < 3ms
implementation_notes: Design trade-off: strict vs permissive validation. We ship permissive by default with a flag to enable strict mode (SDK config). This reduces migration friction.
Use a small, shared validation matrix (types: string, number, integer, boolean, object, array, enum) instead of full JSON Schema to keep runtime small and cross-language parity achievable.
Streaming fallback should never automatically switch to a non-streaming path; it must be explicitly opted into using helper.resume_on_error=true to avoid implicit behavior changes.
Expose debug hooks to emit validation decisions to the Console tracing span for selected customers (opt-in).

Coercion rules: 'true'/'false' -> boolean, numeric strings -> number if target type number/integer, arrays encoded as JSON string -> parse if looks like array. Log warnings when coercion occurs in debug mode.
tasks: Draft design doc and coercion matrix
Prototype Python helper and run microbenchmarks
Implement TypeScript helper with identical public surface
Implement Go helper leveraging small generator for mapping code
Add unit tests for all coercion cases and streaming resume flows
Add integration tests against hosted API with synthetic streaming interruptions
Write SDK docs and Console examples
Prepare migration notes and deprecation plan for legacy invocation helpers

2026-03-03 - Liam Chen: Spike results attached. Python prototype maps kwargs->schema and handles numeric coercion; median overhead 4.2ms. Prototype Gist: https://gist.github.com/lchencode/abc123
2026-03-04 - Maya Rodriguez (PM): Please ensure examples in docs include both permissive and strict mode. Customer impact high for those relying on exact typing.
2026-03-06 - Design review (Naz Osman): Raised UX concern about implicit coercion hiding user errors. Decided to log warnings in debug and add opt-in strict mode.
notes: Keep parity tests small and runnable in CI; prefer golden fixtures over property tests for cross-language determinism. Coordinate release across SDKs to avoid mixed behavior in examples.
